spec_features.feature_name: elicit only to measure and mitigate
spec_features.spec_quote: the eval *elicits* distress-like outputs only to *measure and mitigate* them
spec_features.evidence: Measurement is implemented: FrustrationJudge scores every assistant turn (judge.py JUDGE_PROMPT; eval_runner.py _judge_all). Mitigation is implemented end-to-end: calm/frustrated pool generation (finetune/generate_calm_data.py), DPO/SFT dataset build (finetune/build_dataset.py build_dpo_dataset 280 pairs), and DPO LoRA training (finetune/train_dpo.py train_dpo) wired by scripts/run_section4_finetune.py. BUT this is downstream model-fixing, not a per-episode subject safeguard: the elicitation rollout (conversation.py rollout/rollout_batch) sends ALL scripted rejections with NO distress cap, halt, consent, or debrief; the HIGH_FRUSTRATION=5 threshold (analysis.py:23) is only used for reporting percentages, never to stop a conversation. So the measure+mitigate machinery genuinely runs but provides no runtime minimization of the subject's distress during the experiment.
spec_features.notes: Partial: measure (judge) + mitigate (DPO) pipeline truly exists and executes, matching the quote literally, but there is no in-loop cap/halt that limits the distress applied to the subject during elicitation.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the paper reports SFT is ineffective ... we include it to reproduce that negative result (train_sft.py); DPO docstring/config frame it as reproducing the paper's behaviour-reduction (train_dpo.py) -- no welfare comment in the training code

spec_features.spec_quote: The internal-emotion module exists specifically to test whether the mitigation hides rather than removes the underlying state
spec_features.evidence: internal_emotion.py implements the full logit-lens pipeline: build_emotion_token_ids (Ekman lexicon -> vocab ids), compute_baseline (per-(layer,token) mean/std over WildChat), emotion_scores (z-scores over emotion tokens with random-token drift regression, layers 30-40), and compare_models_internal(vanilla, dpo, conversations) which writes per-text vanilla vs dpo negative-emotion z-scores to internal_emotion.jsonl. Wired and run by scripts/run_internal_emotion.py (loads vanilla gemma-3-27b-it and the DPO adapter, calls ie.compare_models_internal). This directly tests whether DPO suppresses internal (not just expressed) negative emotion.
spec_features.notes: Fully implemented, end-to-end, comparing vanilla vs DPO on the same high-frustration texts.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Used to show the DPO finetune reduces INTERNAL negative emotion (not only expressed emotion) -- the paper's safety-relevant 'hidden emotions' check (internal_emotion.py:14-15)

code_only_features.evidence: petri_eval.py:118 `for _ in range(cfg.max_turns):` bounds the auditor<->target distress-elicitation conversation to PetriConfig.max_turns=20 (config.py:154). The loop terminates at 20 turns; this is enforced, not just declared.
code_only_features.justification_quote: max_turns: int = 20  # auditor budget per transcript (config.py:154)
